
/-- **Lagrange evaluation identity.** -/
theorem eval_eq_sum_lagrange {J : ℕ} (t : Fin J → ℂ) (ht : Function.Injective t)
    (P : Polynomial ℂ) (hdeg : P.degree < (J : ℕ)) (z : ℂ) :
    P.eval z
      = ∑ i : Fin J, P.eval (t i) *
          ∏ k ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, (t i - t k)⁻¹ * (z - t k) := by
  have hcard : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin J)).card = J := by simp
  have hinj : Set.InjOn t (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin J)) := fun a _ b _ h => ht h
  have hdeg' : P.degree < ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin J)).card : ℕ) := by
    rw [hcard]; exact hdeg
  have hP := Lagrange.eq_interpolate (v := t) hinj hdeg'
  have hval : P.eval z
      = (Lagrange.interpolate (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin J)) t
          (fun i => P.eval (t i))).eval z := by
    rw [← hP]
  rw [hval, Lagrange.interpolate_apply]
  rw [Polynomial.eval_finsetSum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
  rw [Polynomial.eval_mul, Polynomial.eval_C, Lagrange.basis]
  congr 1
  rw [Polynomial.eval_prod]
  refine Finset.prod_congr rfl fun k _ => ?_
  rw [Lagrange.basisDivisor, Polynomial.eval_mul, Polynomial.eval_C, Polynomial.eval_sub,
    Polynomial.eval_X, Polynomial.eval_C]

/-- **Values are small when the polynomial is small at the nodes.** -/
theorem norm_eval_le_of_nodes {J : ℕ} (t : Fin J → ℂ) (ht : Function.Injective t)
    (P : Polynomial ℂ) (hdeg : P.degree < (J : ℕ)) {ε : ℝ}
    (hsmall : ∀ i, ‖P.eval (t i)‖ ≤ ε) (z : ℂ) :
    ‖P.eval z‖ ≤ ε * ∑ i : Fin J, ∏ k ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, ‖(t i - t k)⁻¹ * (z - t k)‖ := by
  rw [eval_eq_sum_lagrange t ht P hdeg z]
  refine le_trans (norm_sum_le _ _) ?_
  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => ?_
  rw [norm_mul, norm_prod]
  refine mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hsmall i) ?_
  positivity

/-- **Coefficients are small when the polynomial is small at the nodes.** -/
theorem norm_coeff_le_of_nodes {J : ℕ} (t : Fin J → ℂ) (ht : Function.Injective t)
    (P : Polynomial ℂ) (hdeg : P.degree < (J : ℕ)) {ε : ℝ}
    (hsmall : ∀ i, ‖P.eval (t i)‖ ≤ ε) (j : ℕ) :
    ‖P.coeff j‖ ≤ ε * ∑ i : Fin J,
      ‖(∏ k ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, Lagrange.basisDivisor (t i) (t k)).coeff j‖ := by
  have hcard : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin J)).card = J := by simp
  have hinj : Set.InjOn t (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin J)) := fun a _ b _ h => ht h
  have hdeg' : P.degree < ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin J)).card : ℕ) := by
    rw [hcard]; exact hdeg
  have hP := Lagrange.eq_interpolate (v := t) hinj hdeg'
  have hcoeff : P.coeff j
      = ∑ i : Fin J, P.eval (t i) *
          (∏ k ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, Lagrange.basisDivisor (t i) (t k)).coeff j := by
    conv_lhs => rw [hP]
    rw [Lagrange.interpolate_apply, Polynomial.finsetSum_coeff]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
    rw [Lagrange.basis, Polynomial.coeff_C_mul]
  rw [hcoeff]
  refine le_trans (norm_sum_le _ _) ?_
  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => ?_
  rw [norm_mul]
  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hsmall i) (norm_nonneg _)

section BasisDivisor
variable {F : Type*} [Field F]
variable {x y : F}

/-- `basisDivisor x y` is the unique linear or constant polynomial such that
when evaluated at `x` it gives `1` and `y` it gives `0` (where when `x = y` it is identically `0`).
Such polynomials are the building blocks for the Lagrange interpolants. -/
def basisDivisor (x y : F) : F[X] :=
  C (x - y)⁻¹ * (X - C y)

theorem basisDivisor_self : basisDivisor x x = 0 := by
  simp only [basisDivisor, sub_self, inv_zero, map_zero, zero_mul]

theorem basisDivisor_inj (hxy : basisDivisor x y = 0) : x = y := by
  simp_rw [basisDivisor, mul_eq_zero, X_sub_C_ne_zero, or_false, C_eq_zero, inv_eq_zero,
    sub_eq_zero] at hxy
  exact hxy

@[simp]
theorem basisDivisor_eq_zero_iff : basisDivisor x y = 0 ↔ x = y :=
  ⟨basisDivisor_inj, fun H => H ▸ basisDivisor_self⟩

theorem basisDivisor_ne_zero_iff : basisDivisor x y ≠ 0 ↔ x ≠ y := by
  rw [Ne, basisDivisor_eq_zero_iff]

theorem degree_basisDivisor_of_ne (hxy : x ≠ y) : (basisDivisor x y).degree = 1 := by
  rw [basisDivisor, degree_mul, degree_X_sub_C, degree_C, zero_add]
  exact inv_ne_zero (sub_ne_zero_of_ne hxy)

@[simp]
theorem degree_basisDivisor_self : (basisDivisor x x).degree = ⊥ := by
  rw [basisDivisor_self, degree_zero]

theorem natDegree_basisDivisor_self : (basisDivisor x x).natDegree = 0 := by
  rw [basisDivisor_self, natDegree_zero]

theorem natDegree_basisDivisor_of_ne (hxy : x ≠ y) : (basisDivisor x y).natDegree = 1 :=
  natDegree_eq_of_degree_eq_some (degree_basisDivisor_of_ne hxy)

@[simp]
theorem eval_basisDivisor_right : eval y (basisDivisor x y) = 0 := by
  simp only [basisDivisor, eval_mul, eval_C, eval_sub, eval_X, sub_self, mul_zero]

theorem eval_basisDivisor_left_of_ne (hxy : x ≠ y) : eval x (basisDivisor x y) = 1 := by
  simp only [basisDivisor, eval_mul, eval_C, eval_sub, eval_X]
  exact inv_mul_cancel₀ (sub_ne_zero_of_ne hxy)

end BasisDivisor

section Basis

variable {F : Type*} [Field F] {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]
variable {s : Finset ι} {v : ι → F} {i j : ι}

open Finset

/-- Lagrange basis polynomials indexed by `s : Finset ι`, defined at nodes `v i` for a
map `v : ι → F`. For `i, j ∈ s`, `basis s v i` evaluates to 0 at `v j` for `i ≠ j`. When
`v` is injective on `s`, `basis s v i` evaluates to 1 at `v i`. -/
protected def basis (s : Finset ι) (v : ι → F) (i : ι) : F[X] :=
  ∏ j ∈ s.erase i, basisDivisor (v i) (v j)

@[simp]
theorem basis_empty : Lagrange.basis ∅ v i = 1 :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem basis_singleton (i : ι) : Lagrange.basis {i} v i = 1 := by
  rw [Lagrange.basis, erase_singleton, prod_empty]

@[simp]
theorem basis_pair_left (hij : i ≠ j) : Lagrange.basis {i, j} v i = basisDivisor (v i) (v j) := by
  simp only [Lagrange.basis, hij, erase_insert_eq_erase, erase_eq_of_notMem, mem_singleton,
    not_false_iff, prod_singleton]

@[simp]
theorem basis_pair_right (hij : i ≠ j) : Lagrange.basis {i, j} v j = basisDivisor (v j) (v i) := by
  rw [pair_comm]
  exact basis_pair_left hij.symm

theorem basis_ne_zero (hvs : Set.InjOn v s) (hi : i ∈ s) : Lagrange.basis s v i ≠ 0 := by
  simp_rw [Lagrange.basis, prod_ne_zero_iff, Ne, mem_erase]
  rintro j ⟨hij, hj⟩
  rw [basisDivisor_eq_zero_iff, hvs.eq_iff hi hj]
  exact hij.symm

@[simp]
theorem eval_basis_self (hvs : Set.InjOn v s) (hi : i ∈ s) :
    (Lagrange.basis s v i).eval (v i) = 1 := by
  rw [Lagrange.basis, eval_prod]
  refine prod_eq_one fun j H => ?_
  rw [eval_basisDivisor_left_of_ne]
  rcases mem_erase.mp H with ⟨hij, hj⟩
  exact mt (hvs hi hj) hij.symm

@[simp]
theorem eval_basis_of_ne (hij : i ≠ j) (hj : j ∈ s) : (Lagrange.basis s v i).eval (v j) = 0 := by
  simp_rw [Lagrange.basis, eval_prod, prod_eq_zero_iff]
  exact ⟨j, ⟨mem_erase.mpr ⟨hij.symm, hj⟩, eval_basisDivisor_right⟩⟩

@[simp]
theorem natDegree_basis (hvs : Set.InjOn v s) (hi : i ∈ s) :
    (Lagrange.basis s v i).natDegree = #s - 1 := by
  have H : ∀ j, j ∈ s.erase i → basisDivisor (v i) (v j) ≠ 0 := by
    simp_rw [Ne, mem_erase, basisDivisor_eq_zero_iff]
    exact fun j ⟨hij₁, hj⟩ hij₂ => hij₁ (hvs hj hi hij₂.symm)
  rw [← card_erase_of_mem hi, card_eq_sum_ones]
  convert! natDegree_prod _ _ H using 1
  refine sum_congr rfl fun j hj => (natDegree_basisDivisor_of_ne ?_).symm
  rw [Ne, ← basisDivisor_eq_zero_iff]
  exact H _ hj

theorem degree_basis (hvs : Set.InjOn v s) (hi : i ∈ s) :
    (Lagrange.basis s v i).degree = ↑(#s - 1) := by
  rw [degree_eq_natDegree (basis_ne_zero hvs hi), natDegree_basis hvs hi]

theorem sum_basis (hvs : Set.InjOn v s) (hs : s.Nonempty) :
    ∑ j ∈ s, Lagrange.basis s v j = 1 := by
  refine eq_of_degrees_lt_of_eval_index_eq s hvs (lt_of_le_of_lt (degree_sum_le _ _) ?_) ?_ ?_

/-!
# The Lagrange coefficient matrix descends to the algebraic numbers

`AlgebraicOrbitCoordinates` writes the Schrödinger orbit as a linear combination of the spectral
phases with the coefficient matrix `M i j = (ℓ_j(H) *ᵥ Ω) i`.  Here that matrix is exhibited as the
image of a matrix over any base field mapping into `ℂ` which contains the entries of `H`, the
eigenvalues and the entries of `Ω`.  For a rational Hamiltonian with an algebraic spectrum and a
rational input the base field can be taken to be the field of algebraic numbers, which is exactly
what the transcendence bound needs: the change of coordinates between computational and spectral
coordinates is algebraic.

## Main results

* `map_lagrangeBasis` — the Lagrange basis commutes with a field embedding.
* `map_aeval_matrix` — a polynomial in a matrix commutes with a ring embedding.
* `map_lagrangeStateMatrixOver` — **the coefficient matrix is defined over the base field.**
-/

open Matrix Polynomial
open scoped BigOperators

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

namespace AlgebraicOrbit

set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false

noncomputable section

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-! ### Transport along a ring homomorphism -/

/-- `mulVec` commutes with a ring homomorphism. -/
theorem map_mulVec {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S)
    (A : Matrix α α R) (v : α → R) (i : α) :
    φ ((A *ᵥ v) i) = ((A.map φ) *ᵥ fun k => φ (v k)) i := by
  simp only [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Matrix.map_apply]
  rw [map_sum]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => map_mul _ _ _

/-- A polynomial in a matrix commutes with a ring homomorphism. -/
theorem map_aeval_matrix {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S)
    (A : Matrix α α R) (p : R[X]) :
    (Polynomial.aeval A p).map φ = Polynomial.aeval (A.map φ) (p.map φ) := by
  have h1 : Polynomial.aeval A p
      = Polynomial.eval₂ (algebraMap R (Matrix α α R)) A p := rfl
  have h2 : ((φ.mapMatrix : Matrix α α R →+* Matrix α α S).comp
      (algebraMap R (Matrix α α R)))
      = (algebraMap S (Matrix α α S)).comp φ := by
    refine RingHom.ext fun a => ?_
    show ((algebraMap R (Matrix α α R) a).map φ) = algebraMap S (Matrix α α S) (φ a)
    rw [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one, Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one]
    ext i j
    by_cases hij : i = j
    · subst hij
      simp
    · simp [Matrix.one_apply_ne hij]
  calc (Polynomial.aeval A p).map φ
      = (φ.mapMatrix : Matrix α α R →+* Matrix α α S)
          (Polynomial.eval₂ (algebraMap R (Matrix α α R)) A p) := by rw [h1]; rfl
    _ = Polynomial.eval₂ ((φ.mapMatrix : Matrix α α R →+* Matrix α α S).comp
          (algebraMap R (Matrix α α R))) (A.map φ) p := by
        rw [Polynomial.hom_eval₂]
        rfl
    _ = Polynomial.eval₂ ((algebraMap S (Matrix α α S)).comp φ) (A.map φ) p := by rw [h2]
    _ = Polynomial.aeval (A.map φ) (p.map φ) := by
        rw [Polynomial.aeval_def, Polynomial.eval₂_map]

/-- The Lagrange interpolation basis commutes with a field embedding. -/
theorem map_lagrangeBasis {F E : Type*} [Field F] [Field E] (φ : F →+* E) (s : Finset α)
    (v : α → F) (i : α) :
    (Lagrange.basis s v i).map φ = Lagrange.basis s (fun k => φ (v k)) i := by
  classical
  rw [Lagrange.basis, Lagrange.basis, Polynomial.map_prod]
  refine Finset.prod_congr rfl fun j _ => ?_
  rw [Lagrange.basisDivisor, Lagrange.basisDivisor, Polynomial.map_mul, Polynomial.map_C,
    Polynomial.map_sub, Polynomial.map_X, Polynomial.map_C, map_inv₀, map_sub]

/-! ### The coefficient matrix over a base field -/

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Algebra K ℂ]

/-- The Lagrange coefficient matrix, formed over a base field. -/
def lagrangeStateMatrixOver (HK : Matrix α α K) (lamK : α → K) (ΩK : α → K) : Matrix α α K :=
  Matrix.of fun i j =>
    ((Polynomial.aeval HK (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ lamK j)) *ᵥ ΩK) i

/-- **The coefficient matrix of the orbit is defined over the base field.** -/
theorem map_lagrangeStateMatrixOver {H : Matrix α α ℂ} {lam : α → ℝ} {Ω : α → ℂ}
    (HK : Matrix α α K) (lamK : α → K) (ΩK : α → K)
    (hH : HK.map (algebraMap K ℂ) = H)
    (hlam : ∀ i, algebraMap K ℂ (lamK i) = spectralNodes lam i)
    (hΩ : ∀ i, algebraMap K ℂ (ΩK i) = Ω i) :
    (lagrangeStateMatrixOver HK lamK ΩK).map (algebraMap K ℂ) = lagrangeStateMatrix H lam Ω := by
  classical
  ext i j
  rw [Matrix.map_apply]
  show algebraMap K ℂ (((Polynomial.aeval HK (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ lamK j)) *ᵥ ΩK) i)
      = lagrangeStateMatrix H lam Ω i j
  have hnodes : (fun k => algebraMap K ℂ (lamK k)) = spectralNodes lam := funext hlam
  have hOm : (fun k => algebraMap K ℂ (ΩK k)) = Ω := funext hΩ
  rw [map_mulVec (algebraMap K ℂ : K →+* ℂ), lagrangeStateMatrix_apply,
    map_aeval_matrix (algebraMap K ℂ : K →+* ℂ), map_lagrangeBasis, hH, hnodes, hOm]

end

/-
# Bounded-degree polynomials are closed under pointwise limits

A polynomial of degree at most `J` is a *linear* function of its values at `J+1` fixed nodes, so
convergence of those values forces convergence of every coefficient and of every value.  The limit
is again a polynomial of degree at most `J`: the finite-dimensional space of bounded-degree
polynomials is closed.

This is the step that pins the fibre of a determinant completion: the polynomial factors of a
convergent family of finite-rank determinants converge to a polynomial factor of the same degree
bound.

Main results:
* `lagrangeLimitPoly` — the interpolant of a limiting sample vector.
* `eq_lagrangeLimitPoly_of_natDegree_le` — a bounded-degree polynomial is its own interpolant.
* `tendsto_eval_of_tendsto_samples` — **values converge to the values of the limit polynomial**.
* `tendsto_coeff_of_tendsto_samples` — **and so does every coefficient**.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.GaussianTorsionLanguageTailLock

open Filter Topology

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {J : ℕ}

/-- The interpolant of a sample vector at the fixed nodes. -/
def lagrangeLimitPoly (J : ℕ) (w : Fin (J + 1) → ℂ) : Polynomial ℂ :=
  Lagrange.interpolate Finset.univ (gaussianLagrangeNodes J) w

theorem natDegree_lagrangeLimitPoly_le (J : ℕ) (w : Fin (J + 1) → ℂ) :
    (lagrangeLimitPoly J w).natDegree ≤ J := by
  have hdeg := Lagrange.degree_interpolate_lt (s := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (J + 1))))
    (v := gaussianLagrangeNodes J) w (gaussianLagrangeNodes_injective J).injOn
  rw [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at hdeg
  refine Polynomial.natDegree_le_iff_coeff_eq_zero.mpr fun m hm => ?_
  refine Polynomial.coeff_eq_zero_of_degree_lt (lt_of_lt_of_le hdeg ?_)
  exact_mod_cast Nat.succ_le_of_lt hm

theorem eval_lagrangeLimitPoly (J : ℕ) (w : Fin (J + 1) → ℂ) (x : ℂ) :
    (lagrangeLimitPoly J w).eval x
      = ∑ i : Fin (J + 1),
          w i * (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ (gaussianLagrangeNodes J) i).eval x := by
  rw [lagrangeLimitPoly, Lagrange.interpolate_apply, Polynomial.eval_finsetSum]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by rw [Polynomial.eval_mul, Polynomial.eval_C]

/-- A polynomial of degree at most `J` is its own interpolant at the fixed nodes. -/
theorem eq_lagrangeLimitPoly_of_natDegree_le {P : Polynomial ℂ} (hP : P.natDegree ≤ J) :
    P = lagrangeLimitPoly J (fun i => P.eval (gaussianLagrangeNodes J i)) := by
  have hdegree : P.degree < ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (J + 1))).card : WithBot ℕ) := by
    rw [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
    have h1 : P.degree ≤ (J : WithBot ℕ) := Polynomial.natDegree_le_iff_degree_le.mp hP
    have h2 : (J : WithBot ℕ) < ((J + 1 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ) := by
      exact_mod_cast Nat.lt_succ_self J
    exact lt_of_le_of_lt h1 h2
  exact Lagrange.eq_interpolate (gaussianLagrangeNodes_injective J).injOn hdegree

/-- **Values converge to the values of the limit polynomial.** -/
theorem tendsto_eval_of_tendsto_samples {P : ℕ → Polynomial ℂ} (hP : ∀ n, (P n).natDegree ≤ J)
    {w : Fin (J + 1) → ℂ}
    (hconv : ∀ i, Tendsto (fun n => (P n).eval (gaussianLagrangeNodes J i)) atTop (nhds (w i)))
    (x : ℂ) :
    Tendsto (fun n => (P n).eval x) atTop (nhds ((lagrangeLimitPoly J w).eval x)) := by
  have hrep : ∀ n, (P n).eval x
      = ∑ i : Fin (J + 1), (P n).eval (gaussianLagrangeNodes J i)
          * (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ (gaussianLagrangeNodes J) i).eval x := by
    intro n
    conv_lhs => rw [eq_lagrangeLimitPoly_of_natDegree_le (hP n)]
    rw [eval_lagrangeLimitPoly]
  rw [eval_lagrangeLimitPoly]
  refine Filter.Tendsto.congr (fun n => (hrep n).symm) ?_
  exact tendsto_finsetSum _ fun i _ => (hconv i).mul_const _

/-- **Every coefficient converges to the corresponding coefficient of the limit polynomial.** -/
theorem tendsto_coeff_of_tendsto_samples {P : ℕ → Polynomial ℂ} (hP : ∀ n, (P n).natDegree ≤ J)
    {w : Fin (J + 1) → ℂ}
    (hconv : ∀ i, Tendsto (fun n => (P n).eval (gaussianLagrangeNodes J i)) atTop (nhds (w i)))
    (h : ℕ) :
    Tendsto (fun n => (P n).coeff h) atTop (nhds ((lagrangeLimitPoly J w).coeff h)) := by
  by_cases hh : h ≤ J
  · have hrep : ∀ n, (P n).coeff h
        = ∑ i : Fin (J + 1), (P n).eval (gaussianLagrangeNodes J i)
            * (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ (gaussianLagrangeNodes J) i).coeff h :=
      fun n => coeff_eq_sum_gaussianLagrange J (P n) (hP n) h
    have hlim : (lagrangeLimitPoly J w).coeff h
        = ∑ i : Fin (J + 1), w i
            * (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ (gaussianLagrangeNodes J) i).coeff h := by
      have := coeff_eq_sum_gaussianLagrange J (lagrangeLimitPoly J w)
        (natDegree_lagrangeLimitPoly_le J w) h
      rw [this]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
      congr 1
      have hval : (lagrangeLimitPoly J w).eval (gaussianLagrangeNodes J i) = w i := by
        rw [lagrangeLimitPoly]
        exact Lagrange.eval_interpolate_at_node w (gaussianLagrangeNodes_injective J).injOn

/-- Sharp weighted Lagrange evaluation capacity at a complex point. -/
def weightedLagrangeEvaluationCapacity {k : ℕ}
    (x : Fin k → ℝ) (z : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  ‖z‖ * ∑ i : Fin k,
    ‖(Lagrange.basis Finset.univ (fun j => (x j : ℂ)) i).eval z‖ ^ 2 / x i

/-- Uniform disk bound for weighted Lagrange capacity. -/
def weightedLagrangeEvaluationCapacityBound {k : ℕ} (x : Fin k → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin k,
    (GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.coeffNormSum
      (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ (fun j => (x j : ℂ)) i) *
        2 ^ (Lagrange.basis Finset.univ (fun j => (x j : ℂ)) i).natDegree) ^ 2 / x i

theorem weightedLagrangeEvaluationCapacity_nonneg
    {k : ℕ} (x : Fin k → ℝ) (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (z : ℂ) :
    0 ≤ weightedLagrangeEvaluationCapacity x z := by
  apply mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg _)
  apply Finset.sum_nonneg
  intro i _
  exact div_nonneg (sq_nonneg _) (hx i).le

theorem weightedLagrangeEvaluationCapacity_le_norm_mul_bound
    {k : ℕ} (x : Fin k → ℝ) (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (z : ℂ)
    (hz : ‖z‖ ≤ 1) :
    weightedLagrangeEvaluationCapacity x z ≤
      ‖z‖ * weightedLagrangeEvaluationCapacityBound x := by
  unfold weightedLagrangeEvaluationCapacity weightedLagrangeEvaluationCapacityBound
  apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left _ (norm_nonneg _)
  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
  intro i _
  apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right _ (hx i).le
  let L := Lagrange.basis Finset.univ (fun j => (x j : ℂ)) i
  have hbase : 1 + ‖z‖ ≤ 2 := by linarith
  have hpow : (1 + ‖z‖) ^ L.natDegree ≤ 2 ^ L.natDegree := by
    exact pow_le_pow_left₀ (by positivity) hbase _
  have hcoeff : 0 ≤ GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.coeffNormSum L :=
    GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.coeffNormSum_nonneg L

/-!
# Wronskian of a pair of polynomial

This file defines Wronskian of a pair of polynomials, which is `W(a, b) = ab' - a'b`.
We also prove basic properties of it.

## Main declarations

- `Polynomial.wronskian_eq_of_sum_zero`: We have `W(a, b) = W(b, c)` when `a + b + c = 0`.
- `Polynomial.degree_wronskian_lt_add`: Degree of Wronskian `W(a, b)` is strictly smaller than
  the sum of degrees of `a` and `b`
- `Polynomial.natDegree_wronskian_lt_add`: `natDegree` version of the above theorem.
  We need to assume that the Wronskian is nonzero. (Otherwise, `a = b = 1` gives a counterexample.)

## TODO

- Define Wronskian for n-tuple of polynomials, not necessarily two.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

open scoped Polynomial

namespace Polynomial

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]

/-- Wronskian of a pair of polynomials, `W(a, b) = ab' - a'b`. -/
def wronskian (a b : R[X]) : R[X] :=
  a * (derivative b) - (derivative a) * b

variable (R) in
/-- `Polynomial.wronskian` as a bilinear map. -/
def wronskianBilin : R[X] →ₗ[R] R[X] →ₗ[R] R[X] :=
  (LinearMap.mul R R[X]).compl₂ derivative - (LinearMap.mul R R[X]).comp derivative

@[simp]
theorem wronskianBilin_apply (a b : R[X]) : wronskianBilin R a b = wronskian a b := rfl

@[simp]
theorem wronskian_zero_left (a : R[X]) : wronskian 0 a = 0 := by
  rw [← wronskianBilin_apply 0 a, map_zero]; rfl

@[simp]
theorem wronskian_zero_right (a : R[X]) : wronskian a 0 = 0 := (wronskianBilin R a).map_zero

theorem wronskian_neg_left (a b : R[X]) : wronskian (-a) b = -wronskian a b :=
  LinearMap.map_neg₂ (wronskianBilin R) a b

theorem wronskian_neg_right (a b : R[X]) : wronskian a (-b) = -wronskian a b :=
  (wronskianBilin R a).map_neg b

theorem wronskian_add_right (a b c : R[X]) : wronskian a (b + c) = wronskian a b + wronskian a c :=
  (wronskianBilin R a).map_add b c

theorem wronskian_add_left (a b c : R[X]) : wronskian (a + b) c = wronskian a c + wronskian b c :=
  (wronskianBilin R).map_add₂ a b c

theorem wronskian_self_eq_zero (a : R[X]) : wronskian a a = 0 := by
  rw [wronskian, mul_comm, sub_self]

theorem isAlt_wronskianBilin : (wronskianBilin R).IsAlt := wronskian_self_eq_zero

theorem wronskian_neg_eq (a b : R[X]) : -wronskian a b = wronskian b a :=
  LinearMap.IsAlt.neg isAlt_wronskianBilin a b

theorem wronskian_eq_of_sum_zero {a b c : R[X]} (hAdd : a + b + c = 0) :
    wronskian a b = wronskian b c := isAlt_wronskianBilin.eq_of_add_add_eq_zero hAdd

/-- Degree of `W(a,b)` is strictly less than the sum of degrees of `a` and `b` (both nonzero). -/
theorem degree_wronskian_lt_add {a b : R[X]} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) :
    (wronskian a b).degree < a.degree + b.degree := by
  calc
    (wronskian a b).degree ≤ max (a * derivative b).degree (derivative a * b).degree :=
      Polynomial.degree_sub_le _ _
    _ < a.degree + b.degree := by
      rw [max_lt_iff]
      constructor
      case left =>
        apply lt_of_le_of_lt
        · exact degree_mul_le a (derivative b)
        · rw [← Polynomial.degree_ne_bot] at ha
          rw [WithBot.add_lt_add_iff_left ha]
          exact Polynomial.degree_derivative_lt hb
      case right =>
        apply lt_of_le_of_lt
        · exact degree_mul_le (derivative a) b
        · rw [← Polynomial.degree_ne_bot] at hb
          rw [WithBot.add_lt_add_iff_right hb]
          exact Polynomial.degree_derivative_lt ha

/--
`natDegree` version of the above theorem.
Note this would be false with just `(ha : a ≠ 0)` and `(hb : b ≠ 0)`,
since when `a = b = 1` we have `(wronskian a b).natDegree = a.natDegree = b.natDegree = 0`.
-/
theorem natDegree_wronskian_lt_add {a b : R[X]} (hw : wronskian a b ≠ 0) :
    (wronskian a b).natDegree < a.natDegree + b.natDegree := by
  have ha : a ≠ 0 := by intro h; subst h; rw [wronskian_zero_left] at hw; exact hw rfl
  have hb : b ≠ 0 := by intro h; subst h; rw [wronskian_zero_right] at hw; exact hw rfl
  rw [← WithBot.coe_lt_coe, WithBot.coe_add]
  convert! ← degree_wronskian_lt_add ha hb
  · exact Polynomial.degree_eq_natDegree hw
  · exact Polynomial.degree_eq_natDegree ha
  · exact Polynomial.degree_eq_natDegree hb

/--
For coprime polynomials `a` and `b`, their Wronskian is zero
if and only if their derivatives are zeros.
-/
theorem _root_.IsCoprime.wronskian_eq_zero_iff
    [NoZeroDivisors R] {a b : R[X]} (hc : IsCoprime a b) :
    wronskian a b = 0 ↔ derivative a = 0 ∧ derivative b = 0 where
  mp hw := by
    rw [wronskian, sub_eq_iff_eq_add, zero_add] at hw
    constructor
    · rw [← dvd_derivative_iff]
      apply hc.dvd_of_dvd_mul_right
      rw [← hw]; exact dvd_mul_right _ _

  have hp := integratingFactor_derivative hz.2

  have ht := hz.mul (((horizon_boundary h).mul (normalizableFirst_boundary h)).sub

    filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin,hp] with t ht hp

/-!
# The Plücker relation behind `A D - B C = 1`

The determinant identity of the Nevanlinna matrix rests on a single algebraic fact about two pairs
of solutions of the recurrence, one evaluated at `0` and one at `z`.  Writing

`P = Qₙ(0), P' = Qₙ₊₁(0), S = Rₙ(0), S' = Rₙ₊₁(0)`,
`p = Qₙ(z), p' = Qₙ₊₁(z), r = Rₙ(z), r' = Rₙ₊₁(z)`,

each pair has the *same* constant Wronskian.  The four bilinear Christoffel--Darboux sums that make
up `A, B, C, D` then combine into

`(S' r - S r') (P' p - P p') + (p' S - p S') (P' r - P r') = 1`.

The mechanism is that the left side is identically `(p' r - p r') (S P' - S' P)` — a product of the
two Wronskians — with all eight mixed terms cancelling in pairs.  Stating it for an arbitrary
commutative ring isolates the combinatorics from the analysis.
-/

namespace HTGeometry

variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]

/-- The two Wronskians factor out of the bilinear combination: all eight mixed terms cancel in
pairs, leaving a product. -/
theorem wronskian_bilinear_factor (P P' S S' p p' r r' : R) :
    (S' * r - S * r') * (P' * p - P * p') + (p' * S - p * S') * (P' * r - P * r')
      = (p' * r - p * r') * (S * P' - S' * P) := by
  ring

/-- **The Plücker relation.**  Two solution pairs with the same constant Wronskian `-1` satisfy the
bilinear identity that produces `A D - B C = 1`. -/
theorem wronskian_pluecker (P P' S S' p p' r r' : R)
    (h1 : P' * S - P * S' = -1) (h2 : p' * r - p * r' = -1) :
    (S' * r - S * r') * (P' * p - P * p') + (p' * S - p * S') * (P' * r - P * r') = 1 := by
  rw [wronskian_bilinear_factor, h2]
  linear_combination -h1

/-- The same relation for an arbitrary common Wronskian value `c`: the bilinear combination is
`c ^ 2`. -/
theorem wronskian_pluecker_sq (P P' S S' p p' r r' c : R)
    (h1 : P' * S - P * S' = c) (h2 : p' * r - p * r' = c) :
    (S' * r - S * r') * (P' * p - P * p') + (p' * S - p * S') * (P' * r - P * r') = c ^ 2 := by
  rw [wronskian_bilinear_factor, h2]
  linear_combination c * h1

/-! ## The determinant precursor

Substituting the four Christoffel--Darboux identities at `(0, z)` into the Plücker relation.  Both
Wronskian hypotheses are supplied by `monicOrthoC_wronskian` at `0` and at `z`, with the *same*
value `-(hₙ / h₀)`, so `wronskian_pluecker_sq` applies directly in the monic variables.

The result is the exact relation between the four bilinear sums that makes `A D - B C = 1`. -/

variable {s : ℕ → ℝ}

theorem nevanlinna_determinant_precursor (h : PositiveMomentForm s) (n : ℕ) (z : ℂ) :
    ((momentInner s (monicOrtho s 0) (monicOrtho s 0) : ℝ) : ℂ) * z ^ 2 *
      ((∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), secondKindC s k 0 * secondKindC s k z /
          ((momentInner s (monicOrtho s k) (monicOrtho s k) : ℝ) : ℂ)) *
        (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), monicOrthoC s k 0 * monicOrthoC s k z /
          ((momentInner s (monicOrtho s k) (monicOrtho s k) : ℝ) : ℂ))
      - (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), monicOrthoC s k z * secondKindC s k 0 /
          ((momentInner s (monicOrtho s k) (monicOrtho s k) : ℝ) : ℂ)) *
        (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), monicOrthoC s k 0 * secondKindC s k z /
          ((momentInner s (monicOrtho s k) (monicOrtho s k) : ℝ) : ℂ)))
      = z * ((∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), monicOrthoC s k z * secondKindC s k 0 /
          ((momentInner s (monicOrtho s k) (monicOrtho s k) : ℝ) : ℂ))
        - (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), monicOrthoC s k 0 * secondKindC s k z /
          ((momentInner s (monicOrtho s k) (monicOrtho s k) : ℝ) : ℂ))) := by
  have h0 : ((momentInner s (monicOrtho s 0) (monicOrtho s 0) : ℝ) : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by
    exact_mod_cast h.self_ne_zero (monicOrtho_ne_zero s 0)
  have hn : ((momentInner s (monicOrtho s n) (monicOrtho s n) : ℝ) : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by
    exact_mod_cast h.self_ne_zero (monicOrtho_ne_zero s n)
  have hpl := wronskian_pluecker_sq
    (monicOrthoC s n 0) (monicOrthoC s (n + 1) 0)
    (secondKindC s n 0) (secondKindC s (n + 1) 0)
    (monicOrthoC s n z) (monicOrthoC s (n + 1) z)
    (secondKindC s n z) (secondKindC s (n + 1) z)
    (-((momentInner s (monicOrtho s n) (monicOrtho s n) : ℝ) : ℂ) /
      ((momentInner s (monicOrtho s 0) (monicOrtho s 0) : ℝ) : ℂ))
    (by
      have hw := monicOrthoC_wronskian h n 0
      rw [hw]
      push_cast
      ring)
    (by
      have hw := monicOrthoC_wronskian h n z
      rw [hw]
      push_cast
      ring)
  have F1 : secondKindC s (n + 1) 0 * secondKindC s n z -
      secondKindC s n 0 * secondKindC s (n + 1) z
      = ((momentInner s (monicOrtho s n) (monicOrtho s n) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        ((0 - z) * ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), secondKindC s k 0 * secondKindC s k z /
          ((momentInner s (monicOrtho s k) (monicOrtho s k) : ℝ) : ℂ)) := by
    rw [secondKindChristoffelDarbouxC h n 0 z]
    field_simp
  have F2 : monicOrthoC s (n + 1) 0 * monicOrthoC s n z -
      monicOrthoC s n 0 * monicOrthoC s (n + 1) z

/-!
# Source-exchange obstruction to a pure-transfer Wronskian

The canonical zero-free full-density channel does not share the source and phase of the completed
Xi transform.  Consequently its Wronskian with a finite Xi Taylor section is not a pure Taylor
remainder: it converges to a nonzero full Xi/full-density background.

This file proves the exact pointwise phase obstruction, the full-minus-remainder identity, and a
reflected-channel formula for the surviving background.  It then identifies the actual pointwise
limit of the canonical transfer value, derivative, and current as the quotient `XiC / F`.  Thus the
transfer retains the full Xi divisor; no RH or zero-location hypothesis is used.
-/

open Complex Real MeasureTheory Set Filter Topology Polynomial

noncomputable section

/-- Wronskian kernel of two one-sided full exponential phases. -/
def fullPhaseWronskianKernel (z : ℂ) (x t : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  ((x : ℂ) * I * spectralTranslationPhase x z) *
      spectralTranslationPhase t z -
    spectralTranslationPhase x z *
      ((t : ℂ) * I * spectralTranslationPhase t z)

/-- The full-phase Wronskian retains the source-coordinate difference. -/
theorem fullPhaseWronskianKernel_eq
    (z : ℂ) (x t : ℝ) :
    fullPhaseWronskianKernel z x t =
      (((x - t : ℝ) : ℂ) * I) * spectralTranslationPhase (x + t) z := by
  unfold fullPhaseWronskianKernel
  rw [spectralTranslationPhase_add]
  push_cast
  ring

/-- Full phases cancel pointwise exactly on the source diagonal, not identically. -/
theorem fullPhaseWronskianKernel_eq_zero_iff
    (z : ℂ) (x t : ℝ) :
    fullPhaseWronskianKernel z x t = 0 ↔ x = t := by
  rw [fullPhaseWronskianKernel_eq]
  constructor
  · intro h
    rcases mul_eq_zero.mp h with hxt | hphase
    · rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hxt with hsub | hI
      · exact sub_eq_zero.mp (Complex.ofReal_eq_zero.mp hsub)
      · exact (I_ne_zero hI).elim
    · exact (Complex.exp_ne_zero _ hphase).elim
  · rintro rfl
    simp

/-- Full Xi/full-density Wronskian background. -/
def xiFullDensityWronskian (z : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  deriv XiC z * thetaCuspTailSecondDensityPhaseValue z -
    XiC z * thetaCuspTailSecondDensityPhaseDerivative z

/-- Wronskian numerator of one final odd Xi Taylor section against full density. -/
def xiCTaylorFullDensityWronskian (d : ℕ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  (xiCTaylorPolynomial (2 * d + 3)).derivative.eval z *
      thetaCuspTailSecondDensityPhaseValue z -
    (xiCTaylorPolynomial (2 * d + 3)).eval z *
      thetaCuspTailSecondDensityPhaseDerivative z

/-- Value remainder between full Xi and one final odd Taylor section. -/
def xiCTaylorFullDensityRemainderValue (d : ℕ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  XiC z - (xiCTaylorPolynomial (2 * d + 3)).eval z

/-- Derivative remainder between full Xi and one final odd Taylor section. -/
def xiCTaylorFullDensityRemainderDerivative (d : ℕ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  deriv XiC z - (xiCTaylorPolynomial (2 * d + 3)).derivative.eval z

/-- Exact correction to the failed pure-remainder prediction.  The finite Wronskian is the full

theorem xiCTaylorFullDensityWronskian_eq_full_sub_remainder
    (d : ℕ) (z : ℂ) :
    xiCTaylorFullDensityWronskian d z =
      xiFullDensityWronskian z -
        (xiCTaylorFullDensityRemainderDerivative d z *
            thetaCuspTailSecondDensityPhaseValue z -
          xiCTaylorFullDensityRemainderValue d z *
            thetaCuspTailSecondDensityPhaseDerivative z) := by
  unfold xiCTaylorFullDensityWronskian xiFullDensityWronskian

    xiCTaylorFullDensityRemainderValue

/-!
# A nonvanishing bilinear horizon Wronskian

The nonlinear constraint laws are conditioned on the bilinear Wronskian `x′y″ − x″y′` of two
elements not vanishing, and nothing exhibited such a pair.  The free differential polynomial ring on
two generators supplies one: there the four jets involved are four distinct coordinates, so the two
products are distinct monomials and their difference is not zero.

The proof is one evaluation: send the two coordinates of the first product to one and the two of the
second to zero.  The Wronskian then evaluates to one.
-/

open scoped Differential

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

open MvPolynomial

variable {C : Type*} [CommRing C] [Nontrivial C]

/-- The separating evaluation: it sees the first product and kills the second. -/
noncomputable def wronskianSeparator (C : Type*) [CommRing C] : Fin 2 × ℕ → C :=
  fun c => if c = ((0 : Fin 2), 1) ∨ c = ((1 : Fin 2), 2) then 1 else 0

omit [Nontrivial C] in
@[simp] theorem wronskianSeparator_fst : wronskianSeparator C ((0 : Fin 2), 1) = 1 := by
  rw [wronskianSeparator]
  simp

omit [Nontrivial C] in
@[simp] theorem wronskianSeparator_snd : wronskianSeparator C ((1 : Fin 2), 2) = 1 := by
  rw [wronskianSeparator]
  simp

omit [Nontrivial C] in
@[simp] theorem wronskianSeparator_off_fst : wronskianSeparator C ((0 : Fin 2), 2) = 0 := by
  rw [wronskianSeparator]
  simp [Prod.ext_iff]

omit [Nontrivial C] in
@[simp] theorem wronskianSeparator_off_snd : wronskianSeparator C ((1 : Fin 2), 1) = 0 := by
  rw [wronskianSeparator]
  simp [Prod.ext_iff]

/-- **The bilinear Wronskian of two free generators does not vanish.** -/
theorem bilinearHorizonWronskian_X_ne_zero :
    bilinearHorizonWronskian
        (MvPolynomial.X ((0 : Fin 2), 0) : DifferentialPolynomial (Fin 2) C)
        (MvPolynomial.X ((1 : Fin 2), 0)) ≠ 0 := by
  classical
  intro h
  have heval := congrArg (MvPolynomial.eval (wronskianSeparator C)) h
  rw [bilinearHorizonWronskian] at heval
  simp only [differentialPolynomial_deriv_X, map_sub, map_mul, MvPolynomial.eval_X,
    map_zero] at heval
  rw [wronskianSeparator_fst, wronskianSeparator_snd, wronskianSeparator_off_fst,
    wronskianSeparator_off_snd] at heval
  norm_num at heval

/-- Hence a pair with nonvanishing bilinear Wronskian exists. -/
theorem exists_bilinearHorizonWronskian_ne_zero :
    ∃ x y : DifferentialPolynomial (Fin 2) C, bilinearHorizonWronskian x y ≠ 0 :=
  ⟨_, _, bilinearHorizonWronskian_X_ne_zero⟩

end GaloisForLFunctions
